cases.translation: “If I may take the liberty, your excellency, it would be a good thing.”

cases.sentence: ___ домов, отвалившиеся стены, живописно напоминая Рейн и Колизей, тянулись, скрывая друг друга, по обгорелым кварталам.
cases.explain: «Печные трубы» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: As he drove through the streets past the houses that had been burned down, he was surprised by the beauty of those ruins. The picturesqueness of the chimney stacks and tumbledown walls of the burned-out quarters of the town, stretching out and concealing one another, reminded him of the Rhine and the Colosseum. The cabmen he met and their passengers, the carpenters cutting the timber for new houses with axes, the women hawkers, and the shopkeepers, all looked at him with cheerful beaming eyes that seemed to say: “Ah, there he is! Let’s see what will come of it!”

cases.sentence: Но не успел он вступить в комнату, как уже во всем существе своем, по ___ своей свободы, он почувствовал ее присутствие.
cases.explain: «мгновенному лишению» — after the preposition «по», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: At the entrance to Princess Márya’s house Pierre felt doubtful whether he had really been there the night before and really seen Natásha and talked to her. “Perhaps I imagined it; perhaps I shall go in and find no one there.” But he had hardly entered the room before he felt her presence with his whole being by the loss of his sense of freedom. She was in the same black dress with soft folds and her hair was done the same way as the day before, yet she was quite different. Had she been like this when he entered the day before he could not for a moment have failed to recognize her.

cases.sentence: Она была в том же черном платье с ___ и так же причесана, как и вчера, но она была совсем другая.
cases.explain: «мягкими складками» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: At the entrance to Princess Márya’s house Pierre felt doubtful whether he had really been there the night before and really seen Natásha and talked to her. “Perhaps I imagined it; perhaps I shall go in and find no one there.” But he had hardly entered the room before he felt her presence with his whole being by the loss of his sense of freedom. She was in the same black dress with soft folds and her hair was done the same way as the day before, yet she was quite different. Had she been like this when he entered the day before he could not for a moment have failed to recognize her.

cases.sentence: Веселый ___ светился в ее глазах; на лице было ласковое и странно-шаловливое выражение.
cases.explain: «вопросительный блеск» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: She was as he had known her almost as a child and later on as Prince Andréy’s fiancée. A bright questioning light shone in her eyes, and on her face was a friendly and strangely roguish expression.

cases.sentence: На ___ Пьер приехал рано, обедал и просидел весь вечер.
cases.explain: «другой день» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Next day he came early, dined, and stayed the whole evening. Though Princess Márya and Natásha were evidently glad to see their visitor and though all Pierre’s interest was now centered in that house, by the evening they had talked over everything and the conversation passed from one trivial topic to another and repeatedly broke off. He stayed so long that Princess Márya and Natásha exchanged glances, evidently wondering when he would go. Pierre noticed this but could not go. He felt uneasy and embarrassed, but sat on because he simply could not get up and take his leave.

cases.sentence: Княжна Марья, напротив, вместо того чтоб уйти, опустилась в кресло и своим лучистым, ___ строго и внимательно посмотрела на Пьера.
cases.explain: «глубоким взглядом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Natásha gave him her hand and went out. Princess Márya on the other hand instead of going away sank into an armchair, and looked sternly and intently at him with her deep, radiant eyes. The weariness she had plainly shown before had now quite passed off. With a deep and long-drawn sigh she seemed to be prepared for a lengthy talk.

cases.sentence: Она тяжело и продолжительно вздохнула, как будто приготавливаясь к ___.
cases.explain: «длинному разговору» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: Natásha gave him her hand and went out. Princess Márya on the other hand instead of going away sank into an armchair, and looked sternly and intently at him with her deep, radiant eyes. The weariness she had plainly shown before had now quite passed off. With a deep and long-drawn sigh she seemed to be prepared for a lengthy talk.

cases.explain: «другой день» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Next day Pierre came to say goodbye. Natásha was less animated than she had been the day before; but that day as he looked at her Pierre sometimes felt as if he was vanishing and that neither he nor she existed any longer, that nothing existed but happiness. “Is it possible? No, it can’t be,” he told himself at every look, gesture, and word that filled his soul with joy.

cases.sentence: Наташа была менее оживлена, чем в ___; но в этот день, иногда взглянув ей в глаза, Пьер чувствовал, что он исчезает, что ни его, ни ее нет больше, а есть одно чувство счастья.
